bull.b: Membership expansion and rising dues provide a recurring revenue base, while stronger growth excluding qualified medical memberships indicates improving mix quality. High engagement and increasing participation in ancillary services can support retention and revenue per member over the next several quarters.

The company has moved from deep losses to materially stronger profitability while continuing to grow revenue. Expanding EBIT and EBITDA margins suggest operating leverage and better execution, creating greater capacity to fund clubs, services, and other strategic initiatives.

A visible development pipeline supports multi-year unit growth and broadens the company’s physical network. Management’s confidence in sustaining 12 to 14 annual openings, combined with favorable development opportunities, provides a durable platform for membership and revenue expansion.

bear.b: Although leverage has improved, the balance sheet remains meaningfully debt-funded. This can restrict financial flexibility if growth slows or costs rise, while required debt service may compete with club expansion, reinvestment, and other capital allocation priorities.

Strong operating inflows are being outweighed by reinvestment and other cash demands, leaving free cash flow inconsistent and currently negative. Persistent cash consumption could increase reliance on financing or asset transactions and limit flexibility during the expansion cycle.

The paused rollout delays expansion of a planned wellness offering and creates execution risk around replacing the operating system. While customer engagement remains strong, implementation friction could postpone expected revenue, retention, and cross-selling benefits from MIORA.
